collectedWith: curl of the platform pricing docs page (server-rendered HTML, no CDP needed); Sonnet 5 row parsed from the model pricing table, cross-checked against www.anthropic.com/pricing read the same day
schema: Model operating parameters, NOT benchmark scores. Price evidence only: one row, quoting Claude Sonnet 5's per-1M token prices as standard (not promotional). (Schema prefix must stay 'Model operating parameters' — check-model-provenance.mjs only reads batches whose meta says so.)
note: Anthropic cancelled the scheduled Sonnet 5 increase. The platform docs' own footnote reads verbatim: 'The $2/$10 per million input/output token pricing for Claude Sonnet 5, announced at launch as introductory pricing through August 31, 2026, is now the standard price. The previously scheduled increase to $3/$15 per million input/output tokens on September 1, 2026 will not occur.' So the number batch-10 archived as the promotion is now the list price — the catalog moves from $3/$15 to $2/$10, cache from the inferred tenth-of-input $0.30 to the published $0.20 (0.1x of $2). The gap report's 2026-09-02 'claude-sonnet-5 catalog $3/$15, AA $2/$10' was this event seen from the AA side: AA followed the vendor, the catalog's official row was frozen on the cancelled pre-promotion standard. Same shape as the Gemini cut (batch-37) and the OpenAI reprice (batch-34), direction reversed. Batch-10's $3/$15 row and batch-08's promotional $2/$10 row both stay in the archive untouched; supersededRows routes the provenance audit to this batch for the price fields. The marketing page (anthropic.com/pricing) prints the same $2/$10 in its Sonnet 5 section with no introductory language — two pages, one price.
